description:
Found porting Pl/t/prototype-01.t row 82 (s358, #255). Repro: `early_call(@arr); sub early_call(\@) {...}` — perl flattens @arr in the first call (prototype not yet declared at compile position); v2 emits (pl-early_call (p-backslash @arr)) for BOTH calls because the sub pre-scan registers the prototype before any statement lowers. v1 processed statements in order and matched perl. Fix direction: prototype application should be position-aware (compare the call's source location against the declaring statement's), or the pre-scan should record the declaration LINE and the call-lowering consult it. The row is marked TODO citing this task; un-TODO it when fixed. Related: the s358 _merge_module_prototypes local-wins fix (module merges never overwrite local declarations) — same family of compile-order fidelity, note the local-before-use edge there (a local sub BEFORE `use M` importing the same name: perl lets the import clobber with a redefinition warning; PCL now keeps the local — accepted, warned-rare).

=== DONE (s513b) ===
The same bug as #2871 (filed s512 from the static-parse review). Fixed by s513b: every prototype record carries the site of the statement that introduced it and the lookup answers for the statement being lowered (Pl::Environment parse_site / reg_site). Pl/t/prototype-01.t row 82 (the TODO for this task) passes and its TODO is removed; guard Pl/t/proto-position-01.t.
subject: v2 prototype pre-scan applies prototypes RETROACTIVELY to calls before the declaration — perl only applies them to later-compiled calls (forward call gets \@ ref where perl flattens)
